recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Revisit only if a future build regression removes the generated Element.extension or DomainResource.extension slicing from the StructureDefinitions; otherwise additional source prose or spreadsheet edits would be redundant.
issue_request: FHIR-12061 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core DSTU2 change request asking that DomainResource.extension and Element.extension explicitly expose the standard rule that extensions are sliced by url; the resolution was to document that extensions are always sliced by URL and may be re-sliced, and to update DomainResource and Element to expose this explicitly.
initial_application: The Jira comment cites SVN revision 11243. Git-svn commit b48380f01b10a6a18fa88cbc6f13d7fc8b409b16 is revision 11243 and added extension slicing documentation plus generator logic; its subject says #12131, but FHIR-12131 is an unrelated QI-Core navigation issue with SVN revision 11242. Later commit aed32a0db4637f14a5c7da6cd11c2f18d5625460 explicitly says #12061 and fixed generation of extension slicing.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists Base, Element, BackboneElement, and DomainResource as active normative or abstract artifacts. Current DomainResource source has open value:url slicing on extension and modifierExtension. Current build.fhir.org generated profiles show Element.extension, DomainResource.extension, and DomainResource.modifierExtension all sliced open by value:url. Current defining-extensions source says Extension.extension is automatically sliced by url and extensions are always sliced by their url property with re-slicing allowed. No direct Zulip or Confluence evidence was found that changes this conclusion.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The combined branch received an empty audit commit because the current built specification already satisfies the Jira request.

related_jiras.note: Historical commit b48380f01b is labelled #12131, but the Jira issue is unrelated QI-Core navigation work and its SVN revision is 11242; it only helps explain the misleading commit subject.
